items.title: World's largest freshwater lake is recovering after decades of decline
items.summary: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds around 20% of the world's surface freshwater, making it the most voluminous freshwater lake (Lake Superior on the United States–Canada border is the largest by surface area). This makes the lake one of the most important environments for biodiversity—in fact, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1996 because of this. Yet it has shown considerable decline over the last century, with aridification spreading across East Asia.

For Portugal, this is one of them. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play their first game without him . The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7. Nov. 12—BEMIDJI — It's just a few hours after midnight in Czechia, and Jiří Klíma's parents turn their television on. The Bemidji State men's hockey team's standout freshman forward hails from the village of Suchý Důl, with a population of around 400. Every weekend, halfway across the world, his mom, Petra Klímová, and his dad, also named Jirí, along with his grandparents, are watching the ... "For them, it starts at 2 in the morning," Klíma said. "It finishes at 5, then they have to wake up for work at 6. I can't imagine what they're going through. They show so much support to me. I really appreciate it."

Dan Hicks, NBC Sports' voice of golf, the Olympics and Notre Dame football, died suddenly at 64, according to a social media post from ESPN anchor Hannah Storm, Hicks' wife of 32 years. Storm broke the news Thursday that Hicks died suddenly a day earlier at 64, triggering an outpouring of grief, heartfelt condolences and tributes. "Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness," Storm wrote on social media . Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman U.S. officials say is a Chinese spy has drawn attention to the role of intimate relationships in espionage. At the height of the Cold War, a top official in China’s intelligence agency said that his country would never use seduction to entrap a person. Such tactics might be for the C.I.A. or the K.G.B., the official named Kong Yuan, of the Central Investigation Department, told a group of agents in training in April 1960, but China was guided by principles. He looked at the few female comrades in the audience. “Rest assured, we will not be asking you to go run beauty traps.”

Back-to-back systems over the next few days will deliver the season’s first widespread rain. Here’s what to know about the forecast. A string of storms is expected to pummel California with rain, wind, snow and big waves over the next week, bringing the season’s first prolonged stretch of widespread stormy weather to the state. The storms are arriving as the waters off the coast of California are unusually warm and El Niño continues to strengthen. The climate pattern jumbles weather around the globe, often making winters in California wetter than normal and raising sea levels enough to cause flooding.

Kevin McGonigle finished seventh in the American League MVP voting Thursday, Nov. 12. Houston's Yordan Alvarez was the unanimous winner. When Kalle Sauerland started putting YouTubers in boxing rings, the reaction within the sport was nearly unanimous. Heinz von Foerster thought population would grow exponentially and "squeeze" us all to death. It’s not a new fear. English economist Thomas Malthus —one of the early pioneers in modeling population dynamics—made a similar prediction in 1798, claiming that a rapidly growing population would eventually exhaust the available food supply, and humanity would starve to death. His model rested on the assumption of exponential growth, but the equation is only applicable under specific conditions, such as scientists growing bacteria in a lab in a perfectly controlled environment. Even then, while growth occurs exponentially for a time, it does not continue forever.

SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 10, 2026, 5:26 PM EDT By Barbara Mantel Exposure to light during nighttime sleep may lead to potentially harmful changes in the structure and function of the heart, according to a study published Wednesday in the European Heart Journal. The new study is the first to examine how it also affects the structure and function of the heart.

Cost and access barriers are pushing people to modified use and unapproved versions. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That’s around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of densely written text – much of it in an obsolete shorthand – which is now said to contain hundreds of proved theorems The Austrian logician Kurt Gödel was one of the most original thinkers of the 20th century. His two incompleteness theorems , published in 1931, transformed mathematics and paved the way for the digital age. After his seminal results of the 1930s, Gödel published only a few papers. His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages, and is of great interest to historians of science.

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called Friday's sudden FAA ground stoppage "unprecedented" but said there's no indication yet of an attack. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin called the sudden ground stop of all U.S. flights Friday evening “unprecedented,” but insisted the frightening incident was “not another 9/11.” Speaking to reporters Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration suddenly issued the full ground stoppage, which bans planes from taking off, Mullin pinned the blame on a “telecommunications issue.”

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said during the intermittent outage, controllers could still reach pilots. A communications outage on Friday led the Federal Aviation Administration to pause departing flights nationwide, but pilots were not entirely cut off from federal air traffic controllers. In a Friday night news conference, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the outage was intermittent, so federal controllers were still able to reach pilots. “It wasn’t a complete blackout in communication or radar,” he said. “So we were able to keep some of those communications going.”

Professional long driver Averee Dovsek explains how working on a bigger backswing may create a timing problem if your sequencing is not up to par in the first place.
